title: ～切る — do ～ completely, to the end
summary: Means finishing an action to the end or doing it completely. It attaches to a verb stem and covers both achievement after effort and using something up.

body.p: 走り切る, やり切る, 使い切る mean doing something all the way without stopping, or using everything up. 疲れ切る and 信じ切る show a state at its limit. The past form ～切った is common.
The negative ～切れない means one cannot finish or do it fully. ～終わる just says 'completed,' while ～切る implies getting through effort or a large amount.

examples.ja: マラソンを最後（さいご）まで走（はし）り切（き）った。
examples.tr: I ran the marathon all the way to the end.

examples.ja: 貯（た）めていたお金（かね）を全部（ぜんぶ）使（つか）い切（き）ってしまった。
examples.romaji: Tamete ita okane o zenbu tsukaikitte shimatta.
examples.tr: I ended up spending all the money I had saved.

examples.ja: 難（むずか）しい仕事（しごと）を一人（ひとり）でやり切（き）った。
examples.romaji: Muzukashii shigoto o hitori de yarikitta.
examples.tr: I saw the difficult job through to the end all by myself.

pitfalls: It is not 'cut.' It means doing the action fully.
Do not keep ます: 走り切る, not 走りますきる.
